data_audit.join_policy: Ratings join catalog metadata only by movie_id. User-level splits and test relevance use explicit user_id/movie_id keys. No contiguous-ID or row-position assumption.
documentation_discrepancies: No behavior-level mismatch was found between the inspected Phase 4–12 documentation and implementations for the interfaces used here.

Interface detail: Phase 10 exposes candidate rating estimates through recommend() and has no separate arbitrary-pair predict() method; evaluation enumerates the existing returned candidate scores and reports missing target scores as unsupported.
Interface detail: Phase 11/12 content outputs aggregate movie-to-movie rankings and do not constitute predicted user ratings.

split.method: per-user final holdout after sorting by timestamp, then movie_id
split.tie_limitation: Movie ID gives deterministic ordering for equal timestamps; it cannot recover the true event order.

users_without_any_collaborative_recommen.53: Known user_id 53 has no rating variation to personalize from

paired_comparison_on_same_supported_inte.difference_sign: negative favors collaborative filtering; positive favors user-mean baseline

rating_prediction.unsupported_policy: Do not impute a collaborative estimate when the existing candidate generator returns no score; report it as uncovered. Baselines are also evaluated on this common subset for paired comparisons.
not_supported: Phase 12: their score fields are not user rating predictions.

ranking_evaluation.candidate_universe: All 9,742 catalog movie IDs except movies rated in that user's training partition; held-out relevant items are only that user's own test ratings >= 4.0.
ranking_evaluation.unrated_candidate_interpretation: This is conventional positive-only retrieval: an unobserved candidate is not an explicit dislike, but it cannot count as a known relevant hit. This can understate recommendation quality.
ranking_evaluation.metrics_user_policy: Precision includes every eligible user and divides hits by K even for a short list; Recall and NDCG are undefined for users with no relevant held-out items, so those users are excluded and counted.

phase12_rank_fusion_diagnostics.interpretation: A single-source row can still receive half its reciprocal-rank contribution when both source lists are available; a fallback with only one available list uses that list without dilution. These are current Phase 12 semantics, not changed here.

feature_coverage.note: Missing values mean no usable source value was available; they are not interpreted as evidence that the movie lacks that property.

qualitative_audit.selection_policy: Fixed earlier examples (IDs 3, 4, 5, and 1), one different-genre movie (ID 858 where present), the longest usable plot selected deterministically from metadata, and the lowest-ID movie without a usable plot. Selection used no held-out ratings.
